clauses.reason: Executive Order 10693, signed 1956-12-22 (21 FR 10325), creates under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act a board of three members to investigate the disputes between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad and other carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees (listed in the attachment printed after the signature) and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen; directs the board to report its findings to the President "within thirty days from the date" of the order; and provides, as section 10 of that Act provides, that from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board's report no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the parties in the conditions out of which the disputes arose. No command has its own fixed end date, sunset or termination clause. Later event: the held report of Emergency Board No. 116, created by this order, is dated "MARCH 15, 1957" on its cover, and its letter of transmittal to the President bears the same date and states that the board "has the honor to submit its report herewith." I record 1957-03-15 as the report date (a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report). On that date the thirty-day status-quo period after the report ran through 1957-04-14 (inclusive reading; the exclusive reading ends it when that day begins), and the order was functionally spent on 1957-04-14. Both are spent facts and not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and" "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The number 10693 appears in the table on page 11 of the held text (offset 10583). On that page the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards; 10693 is entry 34 of 64 and entry 34 of the subject list is "Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes", which agrees with the order's title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it against the page image. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective and take effect; the only hit is a word inside another order's subject line), so the signing date, 1986-02-25, is recorded; the filing date 1986-02-26 (the held text prints "Filed 2-26-86") and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 are the alternative readings, and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10693 (21 FR 10325, Federal Register of December 27, 1956), signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower and dated December 22, 1956; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: one whole-order clause covers the heading, the three recitals and the three operative sentences: creation of a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the disputes between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad and other carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees and employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen; the direction to report within thirty days from the date of the order; and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 of the Railway Labor Act. The list of carriers that the recitals incorporate is printed after the signature and continues on later pages; it identifies parties and states no command. The order contains no Defense Production Act sentence and no other command. Later facts: the packet holds the National Mediation Board's report of Emergency Board No. 116 (PEB-116-Report.pdf, front matter and transmittal letter), dated March 15, 1957 on its cover and on its letter of transmittal to the President. The report date is recorded as a later event; the thirty-day period after a report made on that date ran through 1957-04-14 (inclusive reading), and the order is disclosed as functionally spent on 1957-04-14 (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, both dates recorded). Ending: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 revokes the order by number. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (two machine hits) are the revocation note on this order naming EO 12553 and the matching note on EO 12553. The held-text number-citation scan found the number only on the order's own Federal Register page.

savings.reason: EO 12553 attaches no savings, exception or effective-date wording to its revocation list (the held text was searched for those terms). The board's investigation and report were completed in 1957 and the status-quo period ran out in April 1957; the order created no accrued right or later duty. Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, which the order invokes, is not affected by revoking the order.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1957-04-14: computed end of the thirty-day period after a report made on 1957-03-15 (inclusive reading; on the exclusive reading the period ends when 1957-04-14 begins). The transmittal date is not proof of the day the President received the report; the order was functionally spent on 1957-04-14 but stayed on the books until 1986-02-25.
